source_text: An unramified morphism of algebraic stacks is locally quasi-finite.

This follows from
Lemma <REF_0001> (characterizing unramified morphisms),
Lemma <REF_0002> (characterizing
locally quasi-finite morphisms), and
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0003> (the corresponding
result for algebraic spaces).

Let <MATH_0001> be
morphisms of algebraic stacks.
If <MATH_0002> is unramified and
<MATH_0003> is DM, then
<MATH_0004> is unramified.

Assume <MATH_0001> is unramified. By
Lemma <REF_0001> the morphism
<MATH_0002> is DM. Choose a commutative diagram
<MATH_0003>
with <MATH_0004> algebraic spaces,
with <MATH_0005> surjective smooth,
<MATH_0006> surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale, and
<MATH_0007> surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale
(see Lemma <REF_0002>). Then also
<MATH_0008> is surjective and <ACCENT_0003>tale.
Hence we know that <MATH_0009> is unramified and we have to show that
<MATH_0010> is unramified. This follows from
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0003>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
The following are equivalent

<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is unramified, and
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is locally of finite type and its diagonal is <ACCENT_0001>tale.

Assume <MATH_0001> is unramified. Then <MATH_0002> is DM hence we can choose
algebraic spaces <MATH_0003>, <MATH_0004>, a smooth surjective morphism

Since <MATH_0007> is unramified the induced morphism <MATH_0008> is unramified.
Thus <MATH_0009> is locally of finite type
(Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002>)
and we conclude that <MATH_0010> is locally of finite type. The diagonal

is a morphism of algebraic stacks over <MATH_0012>.
The base change of <MATH_0013> by the surjective smooth morphism

<MATH_0015>, i.e., of <MATH_0016>.
In other words, the diagram
<MATH_0017>
is cartesian. Since the right vertical arrow is surjective and smooth
it suffices to show that the top horizontal arrow is <ACCENT_0002>tale by
Properties of Stacks, Lemma

Consider the commutative diagram

All arrows are representable by algebraic spaces,
the vertical arrows are <ACCENT_0003>tale, the left one is surjective, and
the top horizontal arrow is an open immersion by

<REF_0004>.
This implies what we want: first we see that
<MATH_0019> is <ACCENT_0004>tale
as a composition of <ACCENT_0005>tale morphisms, and then we can use

<REF_0005>
to see that <MATH_0020>

It follows that <MATH_0031> is <ACCENT_0014>tale
